Interactions · Interaction of Forces (Magnets) · P3

Magnet or not?

Place two objects beside each other, record what happens, and work out which objects are magnets, which are magnetic materials and which are non-magnetic.

Syllabus learning outcomes on this page (2)
  • P3.MAG.C2Identify the characteristics of magnets.
    Magnets can be made of iron or steel. · Magnets have two poles. A freely suspended bar magnet comes to rest pointing in a North-South direction. · Unlike poles attract and like poles repel. · Magnets attract magnetic materials.
  • P3.MAG.P1Compare magnets, non-magnetic materials and magnetic materials.

See it

What two objects can do beside each other

Put any two objects side by side and only three things can happen: they attract (pull together), they repel (push apart), or nothing happens.

What happens when two objects are placed beside each other
ObjectMagnetIron or steel blockPlastic or wooden block
Magnetattract or repelattractno force
Iron or steel blockattractno forceno force
Plastic or wooden blockno forceno forceno force
  • Only magnets repel. If two objects repel, both are magnets.
  • Attract tells you at least one of the pair is a magnet. Two magnets attract when unlike poles face each other.
  • A magnet attracts every iron or steel block. Two plain iron or steel blocks do not pull each other.
  • Two magnets beside each other always push or pull. No force means at least one of them is not a magnet.

Key idea. Start with any pair that repels: both are magnets. Then check every option against every result, not just one.
